text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Elevated 5xx rate detected on api-gateway (edge) — 12% 5xx over last 3m, triggering page to on-call. Rolling window threshold exceeded.

pagerbot: Paging alice (on-call), ben (backup). Pager sent. Escalation policy: api-gateway/critical.

alice: on it, joining. any initial customer-impact notes?

ben: I'm awake, will jump in 30s. seeing a bunch of 502/504 from the edge proxies to backend pool A. p95 latency up to 2.4s.

carla: logs show a burst of `502` responses with `upstream prematurely closed connection` from ingress-nginx in eu-west-1.

alice: good call. can someone paste a few sample ingress logs (IP, upstream, response code)?

carla: here you go (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T00:15:12Z client=34.103.12.4 method=POST path=/v1/generate upstream=10.4.32.11:8080 status=502 msg="upstream prematurely closed connection" rt=0.012
2026-03-15T00:15:13Z client=34.103.12.4 method=POST path=/v1/generate upstream=10.4.32.12:8080 status=502 msg="upstream prematurely closed connection" rt=0.009
2026-03-15T00:15:14Z client=34.103.45.9 method=GET path=/health upstream=10.4.32.11:8080 status=200 rt=0.002
```

ben: curious that health checks are fine but client requests fail. suggests keep-alive or connection reuse problem or specific codepath.

dmitri: I'm seeing a correlation with a set of client IPs (34.103.*) using long streaming connections — might be sticky sessions. edge routing uses `ip-hash` in that region which can overpressure a small subset of backends.

alice: ok let's verify backend pod metrics. ben, can you run `kubectl -n ingress get pods -o wide` and share counts + restarts?

ben: running...
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=backend-a -o wide
NAME                        READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE    IP           NODE
backend-a-0                 1/1     Running   4          12d    10.4.32.11   node-12
backend-a-1                 1/1     Running   0          6h     10.4.32.12   node-34
backend-a-2                 1/1     Running   0          6h     10.4.32.13   node-34
```

ben: pod backend-a-0 has restarts and higher CPU.

carla: adding that to timeline. metrics show backend-a-0 p99 latency spike and many `RST` from kernel (connection resets).

dmitri: possible root cause: upstream process hitting file descriptor limit or out-of-memory cgroup that restarts long-lived worker, closing connections -> ingress shows 502.

alice: for quick mitigation, let's do a rolling restart of backend-a-0 and temporarily disable ip-hash routing for that pool (switch to round-robin) to rebalance traffic. Any objections?

eve: +1 for rolling restart, but disabling ip-hash will affect session-affinity for some customers (streaming sessions may drop). we should warn affected teams.

alice: agreed. do it in this order: 1) set ingress annotation to change `ip-hash` -> `round_robin` for svc/backend-a (apply quick config), 2) restart backend-a-0, 3) watch 5xx rate. ben, carla, coordinate.

ben: patching ingress svc annotation now: `kubectl -n ingress patch svc backend-a -p '{"spec":{"sessionAffinity":"None"}}'`

carla: done. ingress config reloaded.

ben: cordoning traffic from backend-a-0 and restarting pod: `kubectl -n inference delete pod backend-a-0`

incident-bot: Auto-note: config change made to svc/backend-a by ben.

carla: restart went through. backend-a-0 is back up and ready. no restarts since.

alice: checking edge 5xx rate now.

carla: 5xx rate fell from 12% -> 1.8% in last 2m. p95 latency back to 220ms.

dmitri: kernel logs from backend-a-0 show `OOM killed worker-process` about the same time as start of spike. looks like a memory leak triggered by a particular streaming path.

eve: we should open a follow-up bug: backend streaming handler leak, prioritise fix and deploy. For now, scaling pool + better LRU on long-lived connections might help.

alice: agree. immediate next steps: 1) keep sessionAffinity disabled for 30 minutes, 2) scale backend-a to +2 replicas in eu-west-1 for extra headroom, 3) open an internal P1 bug with logs and heap dump request, 4) notify support with customer-impact blurb.

ben: scaling now: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment backend-a --replicas=5`

carla: done. replicas increased -> new pods warm up.

incident-bot: Customer impact estimate: ~3% of traffic (specific IP block) experienced transient 502/504s for ~8 minutes. No data loss detected.

alice: Support blurb for status page/CS: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors in EU region due to a backend streaming process that caused upstream connections to be closed. We applied a configuration change and restarted affected pods; traffic has returned to normal. Engineering is investigating a memory leak in the streaming handler. We will provide updates." anyone want to reword?

eve: looks good. add ETA for next update: 60m and assigned engineer: dmitri.

carla: monitoring dashboards show stable 5xx < 2% for 10m. I'll keep an eye for any regression.

ben: also added temporary rate-limit rule at the edge for the offending IP range to reduce repeated reconnections: `rate-limit: 120r/s` — conservative.

alice: good. log an incident summary and timeline in postmortem. For now, I'm going to hand off to ben (primary) and dmitri (owner for root cause). next on-call is ben in 2 hours.

ben: taking handoff. summary: root cause suspected memory leak in streaming handler -> caused worker OOM/restarts -> upstream connection closes -> ingress returned 502/504 for clients with long-lived connections and ip-hash affinity. Mitigations done: disabled sessionAffinity, restarted pod, scaled pool, added edge rate-limit. owners: dmitri (RC), ben (oncall follow-up).

incident-bot: Handoff recorded. Pager silence will resume. :white_check_mark:

alice: thanks team — great quick coordination. I'll add links to logs and heap dump request in the incident ticket.

dmitri: I've kicked off a debug build to capture heap on next repro. will update in the ticket.

ben: closing channel for active mitigation. will re-open if we see a regression.

carla: dropping note in #customer-impact with the short blurb.

eve: thanks, closing loop on CS update.

pagerbot: Reminder: next scheduled on-call change for platform is in 2h (ben -> sam).

ben: copy. handoff complete.
